name: Shaman
summary: Among the Horde and the dwarves, Shaman seek aid from earth, air, fire and water. Totems help them wield lightning and ancestral healing as they guide their people. Dwarves follow the path too, as the Wildhammer have long done, and the Skyborne Windshapers seek to restore their people's bond with the winds.

sections.title: Mediators of the Elements
sections.body: Shaman petition the primal forces of nature. Earth, air, fire and water are chaotic, locked in constant conflict. Shaman do not enslave them; they ask for aid and try to keep the elements' fury in balance with the mortal world. Wooden and stone totems planted in the soil help them channel these bargains. Through the totems, shaman protect allies, hinder foes and use cleansing water to mend the wounded.

sections.title: Loss and Rebirth Among Orcs
sections.body:
Shamanism once formed the ancient foundation of orcish clan life on Draenor. Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Council deceived the shamans into war against the draenei, and the elemental spirits withdrew their favor. Stripped of their gifts, many shamans fell to demonic corruption and became warlocks. The tradition came close to extinction.

After the Second War, Thrall rediscovered the ancient rites under the guidance of Drek'Thar of the Frostwolf clan. As Warchief, Thrall revived shamanism and made it the moral compass of the New Horde.

sections.title: Traditions of the Horde
sections.body: Across Kalimdor, the Horde's allied peoples keep different shamanic traditions. Tauren mystics hold communion with the earth and spirits, a sacred anchor of their culture. Darkspear trolls honor the loa and ancestral wild spirits, blending voodoo with nature rites. Across tribal lines, shaman serve as community elders and advisers. They also defend their people on the front lines.

sections.title: Beyond the Horde
sections.body:
The shaman's path reaches beyond the Horde. Wildhammer dwarves of Aerie Peak have long called on storm and stone. Earthseer Farsen brings their far-seeing craft to Dun Morogh, while dwarves of Ironforge also take up the totem and fight for the Alliance.

High above the world, the Windshapers lead the Skyborne in spiritual matters. The wind spirits of Zephras Isle have fallen silent, so the Windshapers train new shaman in hope of restoring that lost bond. Skyborne who join the Horde follow their path.

faq.answer: Orcs, tauren and trolls of the Horde can become shaman, drawing on elemental spirits, ancestors and, among trolls, the loa. Dwarves follow the path for the Alliance, while Skyborne who join the Horde train with the Windshapers.

faq.q: How do shaman get their magic?
faq.answer: Shaman gain power through communion with the elemental spirits of earth, air, fire and water, and with ancestral spirits. They petition these spirits for aid instead of forcing them to obey, seeking balance and anchoring their bonds with ritual totems.

faq.q: Why did the orcs lose their shaman powers before the First War?
aliases: why did orc shaman become warlocks
faq.answer: Kil'jaeden deceived the orc shamans into attacking the peaceful draenei. Offended by the slaughter, Draenor's elemental spirits severed their ties and stopped answering the shamans. Many, left without their gifts, turned to fel magic and became warlocks.

faq.q: Who brought shamanism back to the orcs?
faq.answer: Thrall brought shamanism back to the orcs. The son of Durotan sought out the Frostwolf clan in the Alterac Mountains and learned the ancient spiritual bonds from the elder shaman Drek'Thar. Thrall broke the demonic lethargy that plagued his people and restored shamanism as the heart of the New Horde.
The Earthen Ring is an order of shaman with elders among the tauren of Thunder Bluff. Its members seek harmony among the volatile elemental spirits and heal regions afflicted by spiritual unrest.

faq.q: How does a shaman differ from a druid?
faq.answer: Druids commune with the Emerald Dream, plant life and animal spirits to protect nature's living cycle. Shaman work with the physical world's primordial elements—earth, fire, water and wind—and with the spirits of the dead.

angles.text: As a shaman, your powers come through mutual respect with fickle elemental spirits and ancestors. Keeping balance is your duty in battle and your spiritual burden.
As a member of the Horde, you inherit a spiritual renewal through shamanism, a path of honor and nature worship that replaced demonic corruption.
As a tauren, you inherit generations of shamanic practice and serve as a patient spiritual anchor for the Horde's younger cultures.
As an orc, you reclaim ancestral heritage through shamanism, which helped your people overcome the lethargy of the internment camps.
As a Darkspear troll, you channel the primal elements through tribal traditions, joining reverence for nature spirits with honor for the ancient loa.
As a member of the Alliance, you may see shaman as foes whose totems call lightning and tremors. Dwarven shaman bring those same storm-born gifts to Ironforge's defense.
As a dwarf, you answer the stone and storm, following a path shared with the Wildhammer earthseers of Aerie Peak, who have long heard the elements' voices.
As a Skyborne shaman, you train with the Windshapers, who hope to bring the vanished wind spirits back to Zephras Isle.
